The Missing Principles

Everything the Solen rulebook does not yet say, found by reading the whole estate and then attacking it. Each card is a rule you can paste, the reason it exists, and the proof the gap is real in your code today. Nothing here repeats a rule you already have.

Start here: the 12 to actually do

296 principles were found. Three judges then argued about them, and the honest answer is that you should adopt roughly twelve now, not the list. These are the ones that survived both the ranking pass and the pass whose job was to cut. Everything below this section is reference material for the day you hit that specific problem.

01Make the repo real

Push main and the three missing workflow files. 21 of the findings prescribe a CI job and CI has never run once, so until this lands they are rules about a machine that does not exist. Also make a job that skips its body fail red instead of green.

02Alert when a cron does NOT run

The daily digest only counts crons that ran and failed, so a cron that never fires reads as zero failures. Yours have been failing since 20 July and nothing told you.

03The migrations folder is a history, not the database

Two agents filed a CRITICAL from a migration file that was not true live. Any claim about the database is made against the database, and every audit says which of the two it checked.

04Every ToS promise needs a test

Phone verification writes nothing and the column does not exist. account_warnings has three writers and no reader, so the strikes your Terms promise cannot fire.

05Consent record for health data

Allergies and treatment notes are special-category data under nFADP Art. 5 and GDPR Art. 9. Cheap to add now, a migration against real people's records later.

06Escape anything from the database that reaches a script tag

A salon owner can put a closing script tag in their own salon name and it executes. One shared helper fixes every case.

07Ship a Content-Security-Policy

Report-Only for one deploy, then enforce. It is the one security header netlify.toml is missing and the backstop for the bug above.

08Measure the design floors on shipped pages, not mockups

Home is 4.4 percent imagery, the Basel page is 0.0, against your own 33 percent floor. The PDP passes at 34.7 because it got attention. Nothing measures a real route.

09A law that names a hook is checked against settings

CLAUDE.md says no-decorative-image-gate blocks hardcoded images. It has never been switched on. That gap is the estate's most reliable source of false confidence.

10Shipped means reachable from main

1,686 commits sit on 40 unmerged branches. Two things memory calls SHIPPED live only there.

11One money representation

Bookings are integer Rappen, some other tables are numeric(10,2). Pick one and write it down before a third column copies the wrong one.

12Anything above the [locale] segment is locale-independent

/en/basel serves English text with lang=de and a German skip link, because the root layout sits above the locale.

If you read nothing else

Sixteen things I checked myself this session, against the live database, the rendered pages, git and GitHub. Not agent claims: measurements, with the command that produced them. Nothing here has hurt a customer, because there are none yet. All of it would, once live.

measured Your test and lint CI has never run once, and it is not a settings problem01

Four workflow files (quality, db-migrate, invariants, inventory-freshness) exist on your machine and none of them is on GitHub. The remote repo contains exactly one workflow file, cron-jobs.yml, so GitHub has never had a typecheck, lint, unit, e2e or visual job to run. Those jobs have produced zero results, ever. Separately, even if they were pushed, the e2e job requires STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, which is not in the repo secrets, and the job is written to skip its whole body and still report green.

How I knowgh api repos/sulo232/solen/contents/.github/workflows returns one file. gh run list --workflow=quality.yml returns HTTP 404, not found on the default branch.
measured The one workflow that does run is failing02

The five most recent scheduled runs of Solen cron jobs all failed, in 5 to 7 seconds each, which is the signature of a failure before any real work starts. Nothing alerts on it. The newest failure is 2026-07-20.

How I knowgh run list --limit 5. I could not read the failure log itself: the retry hit a local TLS certificate error, so the cause is not verified.
measured The GitHub repo is 66 days and 1,603 commits behind your machine03

origin/main last moved on 2026-05-21. Local main is at 2026-07-26. Everything built since May exists only on this laptop, which is also why the CI files never reached GitHub.

How I knowgit log -1 origin/main, git rev-list --count origin/main..main.
measured Your design floors are enforced on mockups and never on the shipped page04

Measured live at 390x844: the home page carries 4.4 percent photographic area and the Basel city page carries 0.0 percent, against your own floor of roughly 33 percent. The Basel page has zero images of any kind on a 9,325px page. The salon detail page, the one that got a dedicated design workstream, passes at 34.7 percent. Quality tracks attention, not enforcement.

How I knowgetBoundingClientRect over every img, video and background-image in the first viewport, on the running dev server.
measured There is no salon photography in the database at all05

salon_photos has 0 rows for 28 salons. 20 salons do have a cover_photo_url, and every one of them is a remote Unsplash stock URL, two of them the same photo on different salons. The imagery floor cannot be met by design work while the content does not exist.

How I knowLive SQL against the production Supabase project.
measured Nothing on the site shows a keyboard user where they are06

globals.css sets outline:none on every link, button, role=button, tabindex and summary, for all devices. That was your call about the look, and the code comment says so honestly. What is missing is the replacement: no non-ring focus treatment was ever mandated, so keyboard and switch users get nothing.

How I knowapp/globals.css:387-393, read in full.
measured Every page tells browsers and screen readers it is German07

app/layout.tsx hardcodes html lang=de and sits above the locale segment, so /en/basel serves English copy with lang=de. The skip link is stuck in German on all four languages for the same reason.

How I knowLoaded /en/basel and read document.documentElement.lang. WCAG 3.1.1, Level A.
measured A salon owner can inject script into your pages through their own salon name08

The breadcrumb JSON-LD embeds the salon name with JSON.stringify inside dangerouslySetInnerHTML and never escapes the less-than character. A name containing a closing script tag executes. There is no Content-Security-Policy header to catch it.

How I knowapp/[locale]/salon/[slug]/layout.tsx:128-138, read in full; netlify.toml has six security headers and no CSP.
measured You are storing health data with ordinary account consent09

Allergies, sensitivity logs and wellness notes are special-category personal data under nFADP Article 5 and GDPR Article 9. There are 62 personal-data columns across 37 tables, and zero consent, retention or data-request tables. Only 12 columns in the entire 150-table schema have any expiry or deletion field.

How I knowLive SQL over information_schema against the production project.
measured A gate your rulebook says is protecting you has never been switched on10

CLAUDE.md states that no-decorative-image-gate.py blocks a hardcoded image src. It is not wired into either settings file, so it has never run. You rejected decorative hero imagery three times; the gate written to stop the fourth is asleep. Five more gates are in the same state.

How I knowsystem-health-check.py --report, plus grepping both settings files for each gate name.
measured Two things your Terms of Service promise, the code does not do11

Phone verification: the SMS check returns success and nothing is ever written. There is no phone_verified column on salons at all, so the promise has no storage. Strikes and suspensions: lib/strikes.ts writes to account_warnings at three places, tagged in its own comments as implementing ToS 3.3 and 4.4, and nothing anywhere reads that table. The consequence the Terms promise cannot fire.

How I knowRead both route files in full, then queried information_schema for any column matching verif on salons, then grepped app and lib for every use of account_warnings.
measured A migration would invent wheelchair access for every salon if it ever replayed12

20260530_seed_salon_amenities.sql sets nine amenity booleans, including wheelchair_accessible, lgbtq_friendly and woman_owned, from a hash of the salon id. Its own header calls them cosmetic facets. The live database shows zero salons with any of them true, so it is not live. It is a landmine: any restore or fresh environment would fabricate accessibility and identity claims about real businesses.

How I knowRead the migration in full, then counted the flags live: 20 active salons, 0 true on every one of them.
measured Two of the eighteen critical findings were wrong, and that is the point13

Two separate agents reported migration-file state as live state, at critical severity. Live queries disproved both. I am reporting that rather than quietly dropping them, because it is the single clearest evidence for a rule this estate does not have: the migrations folder is a history, not a description of the database, and every audit must say which question it answered.

How I knowpg_policies for the reviews table, and the amenity flag counts, both queried live.
measured There is only one database, and your laptop has the master key to it14

Supabase lists exactly one project for this account, and .env.local points at that same project and carries its service-role key, which bypasses every RLS policy. So local development, seed scripts, the 21 kill-test scripts and production are all the same live database. There is no staging. This is the finding that makes several others worse: the amenity-fabricating migration, the untested restore, and every experiment run against real rows.

How I knowMCP list_projects returns one project (tocfnsmxmdxkrcmjzzdw). grep of .env.local shows the same host and a SERVICE_ROLE key present.
measured Twenty-five workstreams are marked ACTIVE, for one person15

_plans/ACTIVE.md holds 55 rows: 25 ACTIVE, 7 PAUSED, 19 DONE. Twelve row numbers are duplicated, so several workstreams cannot even be referred to unambiguously. The index was built to stop work being forgotten and has become a place work goes to be forgotten in.

How I knowCounted directly in _plans/ACTIVE.md: grep for the status markers and for duplicate leading row numbers.
measured 1,686 commits sit on 40 branches that were never merged16

Two systems your memory records as SHIPPED live only there: the consistency dashboard (npm run consistency, which does not exist on main) and the Aurora dashboard skin. main itself has 2,416 commits, so roughly 41 percent as much work again is stranded.

How I knowgit branch --no-merged main, then git rev-list --count per branch.

Three things the research got wrong

Out of 21 critical findings, three had a wrong mechanism or claimed a file-level truth was a live truth. All three were caught by checking the running system rather than the file the agent cited. They are here rather than quietly deleted, because they are the clearest evidence for a rule this estate does not have: the migrations folder is a history, not a description of the database, and every audit must say which of those two questions it answered.

corrected A critical RLS hole on reviewsauthz-rls-01
ClaimedThe agent read two migrations and found that a permissive UPDATE policy is never dropped, because a later migration drops a different policy name. Both migration files say exactly that.
ActuallyI queried pg_policies on the live database. The reviews table has four policies and all of them are correctly scoped. The permissive one does not exist live. Real finding underneath: the migration folder and the live policy set have diverged and nothing reconciles them.
corrected Fabricated wheelchair access on live salonsdata-money-03
ClaimedA migration sets nine amenity booleans, including wheelchair_accessible and lgbtq_friendly, from a hash of the salon id, on every active salon.
ActuallyThe migration is real and I read it in full. The live counts are zero on every one of those flags across all 20 active salons, so it was never applied or was reverted. It is a landmine for any restore or fresh environment, not a live defect.
corrected Emails accept a locale and silently ignore itseo-comms-04
ClaimedStated as: the builders take a locale argument and never use it, so everything sends in German.
ActuallyAll 27 builders in lib/email.ts do use the locale. The cause is one level out: of 35 sendEmail call sites, exactly one passes a locale variable and five hardcode the string de, so the symptom is real and the mechanism named was wrong. The corrected rule belongs on the call site, not the builder.

What three independent judges said

The list above was then read by three separate judgment passes that had not seen each other: one ranking what to do first, one attacking the list to cut what is wrong or already covered, one hunting for what a 26-topic sweep structurally cannot see.

Judge 1, what to do first

19
VerdictAdopt about 40 of the 264 findings, not the list. Adding 264 rules to an estate whose named disease is that rules get forgotten or outranked would make the disease worse, and the run's own law-layer-roi-test finding says so. The single highest-value move is making the repository true: the remote main is 1,603 commits and 66 days behind local, three of the four workflow files have never existed on the remote default branch, the one workflow that is deployed has failed its last five scheduled runs, and the e2e job is written so that missing secrets produce a green check. Until that is fixed, roughly a third of the recommendations in this list (every gate, ratchet, lint, axe, audit and contract-test item) are proposals to arm a weapon that is not loaded. The second cluster worth this week is the set of things that are cheap now and impossible later: a consent record for health data that is already being stored, one money representation instead of two, a slug policy, and neutralising the two replay landmines in the migration folder. Calibration matters here: the estate is not broken. RLS is on 150 of 150 tables with 322 policies and no bare true write policy, double booking is prevented by a gist exclusion constraint rather than application code, the booking money path is integer Rappen, hreflang including x-default is correct, and translations are 99.5 percent complete. The failures cluster in three places only: things nobody measures on a shipped artifact, things that only bite on a replay or restore, and legal text that the code does not keep.
do nowIn this order
Make the remote repository and CI real, and make a skippable job fail loud (testing-release-01, orchestrator section 11) ci-is-fictionVerified live: origin/main is at 2026-05-21, local main at 2026-07-26, 1,603 commits apart. The GitHub repo contains exactly one workflow file, cron-jobs.yml; quality.yml, db-migrate.yml, invariants.yml and inventory-freshness.yml have never run because they are not on the default branch. gh run list returns 404 for quality.yml. The e2e job's own comment admits it always reports SUCCESS when secrets are absent, and STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not in the repo secrets. This is first because it is the precondition for about a third of every other item here: secret scanning, npm audit ratchet, axe, target-size, contract tests, visual regression and the lint ratchet are all proposals to add jobs to a CI that has produced zero results, ever. Cost: S for the code change (push, plus one fail-on-missing-secret line). The push itself is owner-only per the estate's own rule, so this is a decision plus five minutes, not a project.. If skipped: Every sentence in the estate that says CI protects this is false, and the owner does not know it. Once live, the first regression that a typecheck or e2e run would have caught reaches production unopposed, and the postmortem finding is that the protection was imaginary the whole time.
Alert on a cron that never ran, not only on one that ran and failed (observability-1) cron-heartbeatThe daily digest only queries cron_runs for ok:false, so a cron that never fires renders as 0 failures. That is not theoretical: the five most recent scheduled runs of the one deployed workflow all failed in 5 to 7 seconds and nobody found out for six days. This is the purest silent failure in the run, and the fix is one EXPECTED_CRON_NAMES map plus one assertion per name at 2x its interval. Cost: S. One query and one map in an existing route, plus one free external dead-man's-switch heartbeat.. If skipped: Once live, the crons that send reminders, settle no-shows, release deposits and reconcile payments stop silently. Customers do not get reminded, money does not move, and the dashboard says everything is fine because zero rows failed.
A claim about the database is made against the live database; the migration folder only answers what a replay would produce (orchestrator sections 2 and 13, data-money-03) migrations-are-historyThis is the best-evidenced principle in the entire run and it was proven by the run itself. Two independent agents on two unrelated topics filed CRITICAL findings that were migration-file truths presented as live truths: the permissive reviews UPDATE policy (does not exist live, four correctly scoped policies do) and the hashtext-fabricated amenity flags (live count is zero true for wheelchair_accessible, lgbtq_friendly, woman_owned, kid_friendly, pet_friendly across 20 active salons). Two agents, one error class, so it is one missing principle rather than two mistakes. It also produces two concrete one-time actions: neutralise the hashtext seed migration and the orphan policy so a replay cannot recreate them. Cost: S. One sentence of evidence law, plus two migration edits.. If skipped: Both landmines are invisible to every existing check because nothing in this estate ever replays migrations onto a clean database. The first restore, branch or fresh environment invents wheelchair-access and identity claims for every active salon, which is a fabricated-accessibility-claim exposure, not a cosmetic seed. Separately, every future audit keeps producing confident false criticals.
Every Terms of Service claim about verification, enforcement or consequence needs an end-to-end test; a clause with no test is not shippable (trust-01, trust-02, trust-03) tos-claims-need-a-testThree verified instances, all silent, all in the place a silent no-op costs most: a legal representation to users. Phone verification returns verified:true and writes nothing; the live schema has no phone_verified column at all, so the code comment claiming it defaults to false in the DB is itself wrong. account_warnings has three inserts and zero readers, so the ToS-promised strike and suspension consequences cannot fire. The cancellation fee is validated against percentage <= 100 while the ToS fixes the platform ceiling at 50 percent and a 24h free window. Cost: S each. One column plus one write, one reader job or admin queue, one numeric ceiling in the validator.. If skipped: The product makes written promises to salons and customers that the code cannot keep. The first dispute where a salon points at section 4.2 or a customer points at section 2.4 is unwinnable, and pre-launch is the only time these are free to fix.
Record a versioned, timestamped consent event for health-category data before collecting more of it (privacy-compliance-03, orchestrator section 7) special-category-consent-recordMeasured against the live schema, not a doc: 62 personal-data columns across 37 of 150 tables, and health data is already stored in consultation_notes.allergies, nail_client_preferences.allergies/allergy_notes/allergy_severity, salon_clients.allergies, waxing_sensitivity_log.notes, wellness_journals.notes/aftercare_notes and spa_treatment_outcomes.follow_up_notes. Zero consent, retention or DSAR tables exist. Analytics consent is a boolean on profiles with no version, no timestamp, no record of what text was shown. Health is named explicitly in nFADP Art. 5 lit. c and is a GDPR Art. 9 special category. This ranks here purely on lock-in: consent cannot be backdated. Data collected today without a consent record is permanently tainted; a consent table written today costs one migration. Cost: M. One consent-events table, one write on the collection paths, one line in the privacy policy.. If skipped: Every health-category row collected between now and the fix has no lawful-basis record, and the only remedies later are deleting the data or re-asking every affected person. At 28 seeded salons that is nothing. At 500 real clients it is a project.
Fix the two live defects in the only customer-facing legal document, and diff the export list against the erasure list (privacy-compliance-04, privacy-compliance-02) privacy-doc-vs-schemaThe privacy policy states Stripe's transfer basis as Privacy Shield, a mechanism the CJEU invalidated in July 2020. That is a six-year-stale statement in the one document a regulator or a customer actually reads. Separately, GET /api/profile/export returns 18 tables keyed on user_id and omits every salon-authored record about that same person (client notes, consultation notes, the category-specific note and photo tables), which is exactly the data a subject-access request is about. Both are cheap, both are text-and-list work, and both are pure legal exposure with no product tradeoff. Cost: S. One paragraph rewrite plus one list diff and the missing selects.. If skipped: A wrong transfer mechanism is the single easiest thing for a complainant to point at. An incomplete export is a failed DSAR, and the estate cannot claim it did not know because the erasure cascade already lists the tables the export misses.
Escape every DB-sourced value that reaches dangerouslySetInnerHTML through one shared helper (input-abuse-03) jsonld-xssapp/[locale]/salon/[slug]/layout.tsx builds a BreadcrumbList whose name is salons.name, a field the salon owner edits from their own dashboard, and passes raw JSON.stringify into dangerouslySetInnerHTML. A name containing a closing script tag terminates the block early. This is the only finding in the run that is a live, reachable, stored-injection vector rather than a missing control, the attacker is a semi-trusted party the product deliberately gives an editable text field to, and the fix is a five-line helper applied at a handful of call sites. Cost: S. One safeJsonLdStringify helper plus the call sites.. If skipped: Any salon owner, or anyone who compromises one salon account, executes script in the context of solen.ch on a public page for every visitor. There is currently no CSP behind it, so nothing catches the miss.
Ship Content-Security-Policy in Report-Only for one deploy cycle, then enforce (input-abuse-05, secrets-webhooks-01) csp-report-onlynetlify.toml sets HSTS with preload, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy. CSP is the one missing header, and it is the backstop for the item above: today a single missed escape has no second line of defense. The research is already done, including the allowlist and the report-only rollout, so this is execution not investigation. It sits below the XSS fix because a backstop for a known live hole is worth less than closing the hole. Cost: M. Mostly config, one deploy cycle of watching.. If skipped: Every future escaping mistake, third-party script compromise or injected inline handler runs unopposed. Report-only also has a pre-launch advantage that disappears later: an empty violation report is easy to achieve with 28 salons and no real traffic.
Measure the design floors against a shipped route on real data, not only against mockups (hierarchy-density-01, hierarchy-density-02, orchestrator section 9) floors-on-shipped-pagesMeasured live at 390x844 on main: /de home is 4.4 percent imagery against a 33 percent floor, 7 distinct font sizes against a ceiling of 4, 42.1 percent of text at weight 600 or heavier against a 30 percent ceiling. /de/basel, a browse surface the imagery floor names by name, has zero images of any kind across a 9,325px page, and renders 56 uppercase elements including the tracked eyebrow the mockup copy rules ban. The PDP, the one surface that got a dedicated workstream, passes three of five. So design quality tracks attention, not enforcement, because check-geometry.mjs and gate:floors only ever run against mockups. This also surfaces a wiring bug worth more than the rule: 20 of 28 salons have cover_photo_url set and the browse page still renders no photography. This is the owner's most-repeated complaint category and the tool already exists. Cost: M. Point the existing checker at three real routes, plus fix the cover-photo render path.. If skipped: The floors keep getting refined weekly while the two most-visited customer surfaces stay at 4.4 and 0 percent imagery. Every mockup passes and every shipped page fails, which is the exact shape of wasted governance.
A law sentence that names a hook file is checked against the settings files; a mismatch is a violation (orchestrator section 6) law-must-match-runtimeCLAUDE.md line 67 and REMOVED.md line 99 both cite no-decorative-image-gate.py as the gate that blocks a hardcoded image src. It appears in zero settings files and has never run. The owner rejected decorative hero imagery three times, the third time verbatim, and the gate written to prevent the fourth rejection is on disk being quoted as if it were live. Seven other hooks are in the same state. This is the highest-leverage meta item because it directly attacks the owner's actual complaint, which is not too few rules but rules that are believed to be enforced and are not. system-health-check.py already finds orphaned hooks; it just does not check the claims made about them in prose. Cost: S. Extend an existing health check with a grep of law text against the settings files.. If skipped: The estate's own law text is unreliable, so every future session either over-trusts a dead gate or re-derives enforcement by hand. The specific cost here is a fourth decorative-imagery rejection.
A workstream may not be recorded as DONE or SHIPPED while its commits are unreachable from main (orchestrator section 5) shipped-means-reachable-from-main85 local branches, 40 never merged, 1,686 commits off main against 2,416 on it. Memory records npm run consistency as SHIPPED 2026-07-24 with four detectors and two live gates; the commit that adds it exists on exactly one unmerged branch that is 267 commits ahead of main. Aurora V2 is the same shape and already known. This corrupts the input to every exists-check, which is the estate's primary anti-duplication mechanism, so it compounds: the next session searches, does not find, and rebuilds. Cost: S. Branch count and unmerged-commit count into the weekly health check, plus one rule.. If skipped: The estate's record of what exists is wrong in at least two known places and an unknown number of others. Duplicate systems are the owner's own named most-expensive failure mode, and this is the mechanism that produces them.
Anything rendered above the [locale] segment is locale-independent or reads the locale from the request (accessibility-02, orchestrator section 10) html-lang-and-skip-linkVerified on the rendered page: /en/basel serves English body copy with document.documentElement.lang set to de, and the skip link still reads Zum Inhalt springen. Same for fr and it, because app/layout.tsx:39 hardcodes lang=de above the locale tree. That is a WCAG 3.1.1 Level A failure on three of four languages, and for a marketplace whose acquisition is organic search it also mis-signals page language to search engines on 75 percent of the site. The hreflang set including x-default is already correct, which is the hard part, so this is the cheap half of a job already mostly done. Cost: S. One attribute derived from the route segment, one string moved inside the locale tree.. If skipped: Screen readers pronounce three of four locales with German phonetics, and the site tells Google that its English, French and Italian pages are German at exactly the moment it starts trying to rank in four languages.
Never set userScalable:false or maximumScale:1 on the document viewport (accessibility-03, typography-01) pinch-zoomapp/layout.tsx disables pinch-zoom for the entire site, with a comment framing it as intentional layout protection. A low-vision user cannot enlarge text anywhere in the product. The stated goal, stopping accidental zoom on specific chrome, is achievable with touch-action on that chrome. One line, no design tradeoff, and it contradicts the estate's own written WCAG 1.4.4 rationale. Cost: S. One line, plus touch-action on any element that actually needed the protection.. If skipped: The product is unusable for a defined group of users, and the estate holds a written rule saying so while shipping the opposite.
A new blocking gate ships with a one-time sweep of every pre-existing instance (data-money-02) money-cas-retroactive-sweepThe money compare-and-set gate blocks future edits and was never swept backwards, so a live instance of exactly the bug it exists to block sits in app/api/cron/pre-charge/route.ts:92-100, updating payment_status, payment_intent_id, paid_amount and platform_fee with no status precondition. This is a money path in a cron, which means it is both silent and unattended. The general principle generalises to every gate in a 164-hook estate: a lock on the door with the burglar already inside. Cost: S. One grep, one precondition, one rule about how gates ship.. If skipped: A concurrent or repeated pre-charge run can mark a booking paid against stale state, and the class recurs wherever else a gate was added without a sweep.
Pick one money representation and write the rule before another column copies the wrong one (data-money-05, orchestrator section 3) one-money-representationVerified live: bookings.paid_amount, platform_fee and net_amount are integer Rappen with the unit named in the migration comment, while services.price and bookings.price_paid are numeric(8,2) and salon_payouts uses numeric(10,2). Two representations coexist with no law choosing one. This is textbook lock-in: a money type is among the most expensive things in any product to change after real rows exist, and today there are almost none. The rule is one line and it stops the next column from picking the loser. Cost: S for the rule and the gate. Migrating the legacy numeric columns is separate and can wait.. If skipped: Every new money column is a coin flip, rounding differences accumulate between the two families, and the eventual migration has to be done against live financial records instead of seed data.
One pass over the five upload routes: magic bytes, EXIF and GPS stripping, multipart CSRF (input-abuse-02, imagery-icons-01, input-abuse-01) upload-trust-boundaryThe same five routes carry three defects, so this is one afternoon rather than three. Every route trusts the client-declared file.type with the storage extension derived unsanitised from the client filename; no route strips EXIF, so GPS coordinates and device identifiers from a stylist's or a client's phone are published to a public bucket; and eight of nine multipart routes authenticate on the session cookie with no CSRF defense. The EXIF half is the one that ranks it here: publishing a location is silent, irreversible once indexed, and is personal data about people who never agreed to it. Cost: M. One shared upload helper applied at five call sites.. If skipped: Home addresses leak in salon and review photos, a polyglot file can be served with an attacker-chosen content type, and a cross-site form can upload as an authenticated user.
Route the Stripe webhook signature and claim failure branches through reportError, not console.error (observability-2) webhook-rejection-alertsThe throttled admin-alert path already exists and is already wired for handler-body exceptions in the same file. Only the two top-level rejection branches bypass it. A rotated or misconfigured STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET means every payment event is silently dropped with a 400 while the product looks healthy, and the daily digest cannot see it because the handler never ran. Cost: S. Two call sites.. If skipped: Payments confirm at Stripe and never confirm in Solen. Bookings sit unpaid, refunds do not register, and the first signal is a customer complaint.
Every sweep claim names N of M and how the sample was chosen; every database claim names live-or-migration-file (orch-output-02, orchestrator section 4) claim-hygiene-sample-and-sourceThis run is its own proof. Three agents wrote conclusions of the shape every upload route trusts client file.type having read four or five, and two agents filed CRITICAL findings from migration files that the live database contradicted. Both classes are free to prevent and expensive to consume: the owner acts on a false critical exactly as fast as on a true one. It is in this tier despite being a reporting rule because it costs nothing and it protects the value of everything else on this list. Cost: S. Two sentences of report doctrine, zero code.. If skipped: The owner cannot distinguish a measured claim from a confident one, so either every finding gets re-verified by hand, which defeats the delegation, or false criticals get acted on.
Decide now whether a published salon slug is immutable or redirect-backed (ia-navigation-06) slug-immutability-decisionThis is in the do-now tier purely on lock-in, not on damage today. There is no slug-edit UI yet, which is exactly why the decision is free: a sentence today, versus a salon_slug_redirects table plus a backfill plus permanent 404s once real URLs are indexed and shared. The finding is honestly marked as not able to bite today, and it belongs here anyway because URL grammar is the cheapest thing to fix before launch and one of the most expensive after. Cost: XS. One decision, written down. The redirect table only if option b is chosen.. If skipped: The first business rename after launch either breaks every shared link and indexed URL, or forces the redirect machinery to be built retroactively against live traffic.
do nextBefore launch, not this week
Ship real de/fr/it for the refundFlow namespace and fail CI on a sentinel key (copy-i18n-01) refundflow-i18n261 of 264 keys in the refund flow are byte-identical English in de, fr and it, with a literal _todo_translate:true marker sitting in de.json ignored for weeks. The refund path is the single worst place for a German-speaking customer to hit raw English, because it is where trust is already strained. It is only in the second tier because it is loud: the first user to open it reports it immediately.
Make the project's named number one failure mode blocking, not advisory (api-contracts-03) discriminate-proof-blockingapi-route-discriminate-reminder.py fires PostToolUse, prints, and exits 0 by design. The estate calls silent no-ops its number one backend failure and enforces it with a note the author can ignore. Requiring a discriminate-proof (a test that calls the endpoint with and without the filter and asserts the counts differ) turns the doctrine into evidence. Second tier only because it needs CI to be real first.
Freeze one error shape and one success envelope across app/api (api-contracts-01, api-contracts-02) api-envelopeFive distinct top-level error shapes and seven success shapes are live, with two of them inside the same file. This matters more than usual here because solen-mobile is a second consumer already: an envelope change after the iOS app ships means coordinating two clients. Cheap now, coordinated later.
Freeze the dozen backend decisions that already have a stated recommendation, and do not build a 15-topic law layer (data-money-01, authz-rls-04, observability-7, api-contracts-10, privacy-compliance-01) freeze-only-decision-bearing-rowsFive agents independently found the same hole: _backend-system has 15 research files and 8 audit files and none of the four root files its own README promises. The right response is not the fifth doctrine directory. It is copying the rows that already say recommended for Solen into one short file so a future session stops re-deriving them, and explicitly declining the rest. The run's own law-layer-roi-test finding is the argument for the smaller version.
Run one real restore drill against a throwaway branch and record the measured minutes (data-money-07) restore-drillAn untested backup is not a backup, and the runbook currently states an RTO nobody has measured. It also happens to be the only procedure that would surface a replay landmine, which is the class the do-now migrations item names. One drill converts a guess into a number and validates the FK restore order.
A synchronous ref lock before any non-idempotent write, not a React state flag (states-forms-05) double-submit-mutexPayConfirmStep already does this correctly and comments why; everywhere else relies on a disabled button, which races a fast double-tap ahead of the re-render. The failure mode is a duplicate booking or a duplicate charge, which is money and is embarrassing rather than merely wrong. The correct pattern exists in-repo, so this is propagation not invention.
A section-level error boundary around any client component that fetches its own data (fe-02) error-boundariesZero componentDidCatch or getDerivedStateFromError anywhere in the codebase, against 171 files that combine useEffect with fetch. One malformed API response in one widget blanks the whole route. ErrorState already exists as a locked primitive, so this is one small wrapper plus placement.
Automatic money movement writes an audit_log row in the same code path (observability-3) audit-log-automatic-moneylogAuditEvent is used at 29 admin call sites and zero automatic ones: refunds from the dispute engine, cron payout releases and off-session charges all move money with no trail. When a salon disputes a payout, the human-clicked actions are reconstructable and the machine-driven ones are not.
Pick one non-ring focus treatment for keyboard users, and report back on the overruled decision (accessibility-01, orch-output-04) focus-visible-non-ringglobals.css sets outline:none unconditionally on links, buttons, role=button, tabindex and summary, for all devices, so keyboard focus is invisible product-wide while SOURCE.md section 16.2 still asserts the opposite as law. I am flagging one overstatement in the audit: it frames this as a legal exposure via the EAA and BehiG, and for a Swiss sole proprietorship serving Swiss customers that binding is weaker than claimed. The real argument is simpler and does not need a statute: a keyboard user cannot see where they are. The owner killed focus rings three times, so the deliverable is one approved non-ring treatment (an ink underline, a background step, a border swap), not a re-litigation.

Meanwhile 21 disposable kill-test scripts outnumber the 6 real tests 3.5 to 1 with no rule about whether any of them still pass.
The booking wizard survives a back gesture and a refresh (ia-navigation-01, states-forms-04) wizard-state-survivalThe wizard is in-memory context only, so a browser or gesture back exits the flow entirely and a refresh resets it, with no popstate guard and no persistence. This is a conversion defect on the single flow the entire product exists for, and it is the flow where users are most likely to switch apps mid-task.
One 404, one redirect decision tree, one meaning per query param (ia-navigation-02, ia-navigation-08, ia-navigation-10, api-contracts-07) route-removal-grammarTwo contradictory not-found.tsx files ship in the same tree, one with a literal em dash and no locale awareness. This is URL grammar, which is cheap to fix before real inbound links exist and never cheap afterwards.

A gift-card email renders the code in font-family:monospace, which the type law retired by name. These are the surfaces a partner keeps a copy of, and they are currently the least on-brand thing the product produces.

Salon owners on iPads are a real segment of this product's operators.

A ratchet costs one CI step and stops the count growing; the sweep is a one-time read.

One page, no code, and it is the difference between a judgment call and an undocumented one.

That is not a gate, it is a toll booth, and it is the mechanism by which a legitimate law becomes something worth routing around. Tying an automatic REQUIRES-DECISION flag to a number is the only version of this that survives contact with a busy week.

Judge 2, the adversarial cull

15 cut
VerdictRoughly a fifth of this list is a real missing principle; the rest is defect backlog, duplicate coverage, or process machinery a one-person pre-launch team cannot pay for. Three structural errors run through it: (1) about 21 findings prescribe a CI job, but origin/main is 1,604 commits and 66 days behind local main and the GitHub repo contains exactly one workflow file, so none of that CI has ever executed and every one of those rules would be law about a machine that does not exist; (2) at least nine findings are the estate's own already-pinned silent-no-op rule wearing new domain hats, and one of them (api-contracts-03) restates that rule almost verbatim while filing it as missing; (3) two agent CRITICALs were migration-file truths presented as live truths, which the orchestrator caught, and that error class is worth more than either finding. The failure mode of adopting this wholesale is precise and already measured in the owner's own audits: the estate has 164 hooks and 410,091 words in _design-system alone, the owner's own CLAUDE.md admits he does not re-read LOCKFILE before a small edit, and one 7-gate family was skip-flagged 72 times in 6 days. Adding 264 rules to a corpus nobody re-reads is a write-only operation; adding the gates to enforce them converts the skip flag into the normal workflow. The genuinely valuable output of this run is not the rule list, it is five measured facts: CI has never run, the remote is 66 days stale, the shipped browse pages sit at 4.4% and 0.0% imagery against a 33% floor, health data is stored with no consent record, and the ToS promises two things the code does not do.
What happens if you adopt all of itConcretely: 264 findings at roughly 90 words of paste-ready rule text each is about 24,000 new words, a 6% increase on the 410,091 words already in _design-system top-level markdown (measured this session with wc -w). That number understates the damage, because the binding constraint here is not disk, it is what gets re-read. The project CLAUDE.md says so in its own voice, as the stated reason its ten taste rules were duplicated inline: SOURCE.md and LOCKFILE hold the full system, but they are 80KB+ and I do not re-read them before a small edit, so I drift. Adding 264 rows to a corpus whose own author has documented that he cannot re-read it is a write-only operation, and this run has already added 896KB across 28 JSON files under _design-system/research/ before a single rule was adopted. The gate side is worse and is already measured. The estate has 164 wired hooks (134 global plus 30 project). This estate's own standing policy is that a rule it keeps breaking becomes a hook, not advice, so on past behavior roughly a quarter of adopted rules become gates: 264 findings at a 25% gate rate is +66 hooks, taking the estate to about 230. The current cost of 164 is already documented: the 2026-07-10 governance audit found 13 or more independently-registered PreToolUse gates each denying one at a time on a single mockup Write, and the 2026-07-25 self-audit found one 7-gate family skip-flagged 72 times in 6 days plus finish-autonomously-skip 40 times. Skip-flag pressure scales with the number of gates that can fire on the same action, so a 40% increase in gate count on the same handful of actions plausibly pushes that family past 100 skips a week, at which point touching the flag IS the workflow and the gate enforces nothing. There is a second-order cost that is already visible: 8 gates sit on disk unwired while the law text cites one of them (no-decorative-image-gate.py, written after the owner rejected decorative imagery three times) as though it were live. Every rule added without wiring widens that gap between what the law claims and what runs, and this run found that gap is already the estate's most reliable source of false confidence. RECOMMENDED ABSORPTION RATE: 12 to 18 principles now, roughly 5 to 7 percent of the list, and specifically the ten merged principles above plus the health-data consent gap and the two Terms of Service promises the code does not keep. Zero new gate FILES until origin/main is current and the 8 orphaned gates are either wired or deleted, then strict one-in-one-out. Everything else on this list is a defect backlog, not law: about 60 of these findings are single bugs with a known one-line fix (the JSON-LD escape, the html lang attribute, the viewport meta, the second not-found.tsx, the webhook default case, the monospace voucher code, the raw email in a log line), and filing a bug as a principle is how a law estate reaches 410,000 words while the two most-visited shipped pages sit at 4.4 and 0.0 percent imagery.
cutWrong, already covered, or already rejected by you
accessibility-01REJECTED. This re-proposes a visible focus state on interactive chrome, a decision the owner has killed by name at least three times, once while (the code's own words) furious and repeating himself. The finding's escape hatch ('if a ring stays banned, ONE approved non-ring substitute') is still re-litigating a settled call, and a live gate exists specifically to block it. Proof: app/globals.css:377-392 carries the dated owner decisions in the comment itself: 'Owner 2026-07-01 (furious, repeated): NO focus ring on interactive chrome, on ANY device' and 'BELT-AND-SUSPENDERS (owner 2026-07-02, furious repeat)'. The comment already records the exact a11y cost the finding claims to discover: '(a11y note: this drops the WCAG 2.4.7 keyboard focus indicator on chrome, owner call ... and the no-focus-ring-gate blocks re-adding a ring.)'. _design-system/REMOVED.md:34 and :35 are two further dated rejections, :34 ending 'Do NOT re-add a focus ring to THIS input despite the LOCKFILE inputs-get-an-ink-halo rule.' What DOES survive here is a one-line doc fix, not a principle: the CLAUDE.md design-contract focus row still says 'buttons/links: the global 2px ink outline', which globals.css deleted. That contradiction belongs in the merge group on doc-vs-runtime drift, not in a new a11y law.
imagery-icons-04ALREADY COVERED. The finding says 'ALREADY: none'. The rule is locked in LOCKFILE. This is 35 unfixed violations of an existing law, which is a defect ticket, not a missing principle. Proof: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md:1149: '| **Single image-CDN pipeline** | All images route through `next/image` + Supabase Storage. Mirror Uber's `cn-geo1.uber.com/image-proc` pattern. |'. The agent's own absence-proof grepped the component tree and package.json, not LOCKFILE section 16.
responsive-desktop-10WRONG. The proof is false. It claims a grep for window.print and 'Drucken' across app/ returns zero hits and concludes 'no print feature exists yet to test against'. A print feature does exist, on a financial document, and another agent in this same run found it. Proof: grep -rn 'window.print' app/ returns app/api/salon/invoices/[payoutId]/route.ts:59: `<button onclick="window.print()" style="...background: #C05038...">Drucken / PDF speichern</button>`. That is the salon commission payout statement. color-tokens-02 cites the same line for the off-palette hex. So print is in scope today, on the one surface where getting it wrong costs a partner relationship, and the finding's own recommendation ('say print is out of scope') would write a false statement into the docs. The real principle is color-tokens-02's (surfaces that generate their own HTML outside the React tree are outside every system), which already covers this file.
hierarchy-density-07REJECTED by the estate's own evidence, and the finding quotes the rejection in its own proof. It asks for a measured maximum share of chromatic pixels; the estate's own research file already recorded that no source supports a chroma count or share as a floor or ceiling. Proof: The finding's PROOF is verbatim: 'TASTE_RANGE.md NOT-SUPPORTED item 7, verbatim: No evidence that a COUNT of chromatic colours is a floor. FLATNESS_DIAGNOSIS counted 2 on home and 3 on PDP and read it as a symptom... no source states a minimum number of hues a screen needs.' Proposing a number the estate already filed under NOT-SUPPORTED is how an unsourced literal enters the LOCKFILE and then gets enforced for a year. Rule 15 (attach a checkable source or cut the number) applies to the estate's own rules, not only to persuasion stats.
secrets-webhooks-09ALREADY COVERED, self-admitted in the finding's own ALREADY field. It is a one-line bug with a known fix sitting in an audit row, filed as a missing principle to fill a quota. Proof: The finding's own ALREADY field: 'full: both the research (webhooks.md section 6) and the audit (audit/webhooks.md WEBHOOK-06 row) already name this exact gap with the exact one-line fix. This finding is included here only because...'. Adding a rule that a switch needs a default case, when the missing default is already a numbered audit row with the fix written, buys nothing. Add the default case.
input-abuse-05ALREADY COVERED and a duplicate. Same rule as secrets-webhooks-01 (ship CSP report-only, then enforce), from the same source file, in the same run. The finding's own ALREADY field says the analysis is complete. Proof: input-abuse-05 ALREADY: 'full analysis already exists and is high quality: security.md section 6 names this the single highest-value gap this file found, gives a concrete rollout plan (report-only first, explicit allowlist...)'. secrets-webhooks-01 ALREADY: 'Full: _backend-system/research/security.md section 6 already researched this exhaustively'. Two agents rediscovered one already-written, already-recommended decision. Keep secrets-webhooks-01 as the single carrier and drop this one; neither is a missing principle, both are an unexecuted decision.
accessibility-03DUPLICATE of typography-01. Identical file, identical lines, identical rule (never set userScalable:false / maximumScale<=1 on the root viewport). Two agents, one defect. Proof: accessibility-03 PROOF: 'app/layout.tsx:29-32: export const viewport: Viewport = { ..., maximumScale: 1, userScalable: false, viewportFit: "cover" }'. typography-01 PROOF: 'app/layout.tsx lines 28-34: export const viewport: Viewport = { width: "device-width", initialScale: 1, maximumScale: 1, userScalable: false, ... }'. Keep typography-01 (it also names the SOURCE.md section 16 gap where the rule belongs). Note this is one three-line edit, not a law.
api-contracts-03ALREADY COVERED, almost word for word, by the project CLAUDE.md's own pinned Silent no-ops block. The finding's actual delta is enforcement strength (informational reminder versus blocking gate), which is a gate-tuning decision, not a missing principle. Proof: Project CLAUDE.md, pinned block 'Silent no-ops': 'Prove behavior, not existence. A filter must DISCRIMINATE (return a correct subset), not just render or return 200. A column must appear in the LIVE snapshot (npm run exists <column>), not merely in a TS type.' That is the rule the finding proposes. The finding's own ALREADY field concedes it: 'the hook exists and correctly names the exact failure mode and the exact three-part proof procedure'. This belongs in merge group A as evidence of scope, not as a new row.
orch-output-12ALREADY COVERED. This is a one-word disambiguation of an existing memory file, promoted to a principle. The finding's own proof is that memory/user.md already says the thing and is slightly ambiguous. Proof: orch-output-12 PROOF: 'memory/user.md records "Colloquial shorthand; match register", which is one sentence and is ambiguous exactly where it matters: match the REGISTER, or match the FORM.' The fix is to edit that sentence to read 'match register, never mirror the shorthand'. Editing an existing memory line is not adopting a principle, and filing it as one inflates the list's count.
testing-release-08WRONG PREMISE. It argues that CI validates a `next start` artifact rather than the Netlify-built one. There is no CI. The distinction it draws cannot matter until a workflow actually runs, and building the rule now would encode a comparison between two things, one of which has never executed. Proof: gh api repos/sulo232/solen/contents/.github/workflows returns exactly one file, cron-jobs.yml (orchestrator live verification section 11). Locally `ls .github/workflows/` returns five files including quality.yml, which contains the visual job this finding critiques. `gh run list --workflow=quality.yml` returns HTTP 404, 'not found on the default branch'. git rev-list --count origin/main..main = 1604, verified this session. The visual job has produced zero runs ever, against either artifact.
layout-geometry-07WRONG. No defect is demonstrated. The proof describes two buttons using standard flex centering and calls the absence of a per-typeface tuning constant the bug, with no measurement showing the text actually sits low. This is a rule invented from a plausible mechanism, which is the exact failure mode the estate bans elsewhere (measure, do not eyeball). Proof: layout-geometry-07 PROOF in full: 'The system's two highest-traffic commit buttons (PayConfirmStep.tsx and BookingPaymentForm.tsx, both 52px ink pills) use plain flex items-center with no per-typeface tuning value defined anywhere to check text position against.' There is no measured cap-top or baseline gap, no screenshot, no owner complaint. Compare the estate's own binary trigger: measurement-complaint words fire a live rect measurement BEFORE editing. A rule proposing per-typeface baseline tuning on 164 hooks' worth of existing law, with zero measured pixels behind it, is the definition of a rule that will be skip-flagged.
layout-geometry-10ALREADY COVERED, and the finding concedes it. The container padding values are frozen literals in LOCKFILE section 7. A derived ratio rule cannot bind anything the literals do not already bind, and its own proof shows the existing surfaces disagree (1.14x, 1.5x, 2x), so the new rule would immediately need three recorded exceptions. Proof: layout-geometry-10 ALREADY: 'partial: the table itself is locked as frozen literals, so the VALUES are law; the delta is the missing rationale/ratio'. Its PROOF enumerates three different existing ratios in the locked table (Page 1.5x/2x, Hero 1.14x, PDP 1.5x, /business 2x, FAQ 2x). A ratio band that three of five locked rows already violate is not a rule, it is a documentation note. Precedence chain tier 3 (LOCKFILE frozen literals) already wins over it.
color-tokens-09Fails the list's own ROI test, with no incident behind it. It proposes tracking and capping the total color-token count. No drift, bug, or owner complaint is cited as caused by the count; the cited number (47) is presented as suspicious rather than as harmful. Proof: color-tokens-09 ALREADY: 'none for color specifically; the pattern exists for radius/duration/easing'. Its PROOF is a bare count: "grep -oE '\"s-[a-zA-Z0-9-]+\"' tailwind.config.js | sort -u | wc -l = 47 distinct top-level tokens today". Meanwhile law-layer-roi-test, in this same list and marked critical, demands that a new law name 'the specific, counted incidents it would have prevented in the last 90 days'. This finding names zero. The real color-token problem is already covered by color-tokens-06 (17 tokens with zero live usage) which does have evidence; a count ceiling adds a second rule on top of it.
ethics-psychology-01ALREADY COVERED, and the existing rule is stricter than the law being cited. Adding a Swiss PBV citation to a rule that already exceeds PBV is a footnote, not a principle. The finding admits this. Proof: ethics-psychology-01 ALREADY: 'partial: PSYCHOLOGY.md law 5 and hard line 3 already require total-price-from-step-one as a conversion law, and in spirit it is stricter than PBV's minimum. The gap is that the file never names PBV'. A rule that already binds tighter than the statute does not become more enforceable by naming the statute. If the owner wants the citation for defensibility, it is a one-line edit to PSYCHOLOGY.md law 5, not a new law.
ethics-psychology-04ALREADY COVERED, same shape as ethics-psychology-01 and conceded in the same words: the shipped default already satisfies the statute being cited. Proof: ethics-psychology-04 ALREADY: 'partial: the current default (marketing off, transactional on) already matches what UWG Art. 3(1)(o) requires, and the same 2026-07-07 audit already separately found the underlying enforcement is broken'. The real defect here is the broken enforcement, which is ethics-psychology-02's consent-flag-has-no-reader finding, which belongs in merge group A. The UWG citation adds a sentence to PSYCHOLOGY.md law 14 and nothing else.
overstatedReal, but not as severe as claimed
imagery-icons-01 high to medium, and timed to the first real salon uploadEXIF/GPS stripping matters when users upload photos. Live database check: salon_photos has 0 rows across all 28 salons, and every cover image that does render is a remote Unsplash URL (orchestrator live verification section 9). There is no user-uploaded photo in the system to leak GPS from. This must land before the first real salon uploads a gallery, which is a launch-blocker slot, not a today slot.
imagery-icons-02 high to low now, medium at first external onboardingPre-publish moderation for a marketplace with 28 owner-seeded salons, zero real customers, and 0 rows in salon_photos is textbook premature machinery, which is a named failure mode in this estate. A moderation queue with nothing in it is a surface the owner has to maintain for no signal. The honest rule is a trigger, not a build: wire moderation the same week the first non-owner account can upload.
imagery-icons-07 medium to lowSame reason as imagery-icons-02. A rights/consent attestation checkbox protects against a third party uploading someone else's photo. There is no third party yet and no photo yet. Merge it into the upload-pipeline work item rather than carrying it as its own principle.
input-abuse-03 high to high but not currently exploitable, and that distinction must be statedThe finding is technically correct and the fix is cheap, so keep it. But calling it a 'live stored-XSS vector' overstates today's reality: the injection point is salons.name, editable only by an approved salon owner, and all 28 salons are seeded by the owner himself. Nobody hostile can currently write that column. The correct framing under the pre-launch rule is 'would break the day a third party can edit a salon name', not 'is being exploited'. Same correction applies to input-abuse-01 (multipart CSRF) and input-abuse-02 (magic bytes).
authz-rls-05 high, effort L to medium, and only the NEW-call-site halfIt proposes a recurring quarterly sampling audit of 10% of 270 createAdminSupabaseClient call sites, for a solo operator. That is an SRE ritual with no SRE. The half that survives is cheap and forward-looking: every NEW admin-client call site carries a visible ownership assertion immediately before the privileged query. Auditing the existing 270 on a calendar is a process the owner will run once and then skip-flag forever.
accessibility-04 high to lowZero landmarks across 49 dashboard pages used today by zero real salon owners. The argument in the rule ('dashboard staff are real end users') is correct and the fix is cheap, but a high severity here competes for attention with health data stored without consent and a ToS promise the code does not keep. This is launch-hygiene, not a current defect.
fe-04 high to low until CI existsThe rule is 'run jscpd in CI alongside the drift-checker'. CI has never executed a single run (origin/main is 1,604 commits behind and hosts one workflow file). A duplication scanner that cannot run is not a gate, and the history it cites (5 manually-found duplicate components) was all caught without it. Blocked on merge group B's prerequisite.
fe-05 medium to lowA 400-line file ceiling with an 800-line debt ledger is generic large-team hygiene imported wholesale. The named offender, SearchTemplate.tsx at 2375 lines, is a real problem but it is a refactor ticket with a name, not a rule that needs to bind 422 other files. The estate already has a decomposition backlog mechanism (_tasks/INCOMPLETE_FEATURES.md); use it.
testing-release-04 medium to lowA 30-day lifecycle policy for 21 one-off kill-test scripts is housekeeping dressed as law. The scripts cost nothing sitting in scripts/, they are not imported, and the stated harm (a future session might think they still pass) is speculative. Delete them in one commit or leave them; either way it is not a principle.
motion-09 low to dropDevice-capability motion tiering (reading hardwareConcurrency/deviceMemory to drop blur and springs) is confidence-tier 'assume' with no measured jank on any device. prefers-reduced-motion is already wired at 11 sites. Adding a second, heuristic motion-degradation path to a system that already has locked motion-22 vocabulary is new surface with no evidence of need.
responsive-desktop-05 medium to lowTablet design intent for a mobile-first Swiss booking product pre-launch. The finding's own proof is that tablet has automated regression screenshots (so drift is caught) and zero documented intent. Documenting 'tablet is a wider mobile' is a one-line note. The same downgrade applies to responsive-desktop-07 (the 1024-1279px zone) and responsive-desktop-09 (pointer vs touch umbrella rule): all three are documentation of existing behavior, not missing law.
orch-output-07 medium to low, and reframe or dropReporting subagent token cost at the close of every large fan-out sits directly against the owner's own recorded preference (feedback_optimize_for_best_not_cheap: optimize for BEST work; only the commit/push rules are hard constraints). The finding anticipates this and argues cost must be visible in order to be traded off, which is fair, but the practical result is a cost line in every large turn, which reads as the budget-consciousness the owner rejected. If kept, scope it to turns the owner explicitly asks about, not to every fan-out.
law-layer-roi-test critical to highThis is the single most valuable meta-finding in the run and I want it adopted, but it is not critical in the sense the other criticals are: nothing is currently broken for a user because of it. Ranking a governance test at the same level as 'the ToS promises phone verification the code never records' mis-signals what to do first. Adopt it, rank it below the live defects, and note the irony that adopting this list wholesale would itself fail this test.
copy-i18n-11 medium to lowConfidence tier is 'assume' and the content is legal interpretation of when 'ab CHF' may prefix a price under Swiss price-display rules, with no cited PBV article text and no owner or lawyer in the loop.
